## Learning Objectives

-   Difference of two means

-   Comparing many means with ANOVA

## Difference of two means

Each year the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) releases fuel economy data on cars manufactured in that year. Below are summary statistics on fuel efficiency (in miles/gallon) from independent random samples of cars with manual and automatic transmissions manufactured in 2012. Do these data provide strong evidence of a difference between the average fuel efficiency of cars with manual and automatic transmissions in terms of their average city mileage? Assume that conditions for inference are satisfied.

```{r}
# loading the data from csv file
df <- read.csv("mileage.csv")
glimpse(df)

summary(df$gpa)
unique(df$major)


```

We can assume that the data are independent within and between the two groups, because the data come from independent random samples.

\
We are going to get each transmission group.

```{r}

Manual_df <- df %>% filter(transmission=="Manual")
Automatic_df <- df %>% filter(transmission=="Automatic")

summary(Manual_df)
summary(Automatic_df)

```

We will make histogram for both groups.

```{r}
ggplot(data=Manual_df, aes(x=mileage)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5)

# Suggested bins based on Sturges' rule: ceiling(log2(n) + 1)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data=Automatic_df, aes(x=mileage)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5)


```

We can obtain the test statistic.

```{r}
# hypothesis 
# H_0 : mu_manual - mu_auto = 0

# Sample mean and standard deviation
xbar1 <- mean(Manual_df$mileage)
xbar2 <- mean(Automatic_df$mileage)

s1 <- sd(Manual_df$mileage)
s2 <- sd(Automatic_df$mileage)

n1 <- length(Manual_df$mileage)
n2 <- length(Automatic_df$mileage)
  
SE <- sqrt( s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2 )
  
Test_stat <- (xbar1-xbar2)-0 / SE


# ---- Test statistic and p-value ----

SE
Test_stat
(1-pt(Test_stat, n1-1))*2 
```

Based on the p-value, we conclude that there is strong evidence at the 0.05 significance level to suggest a difference in the average city mileage between cars with manual and automatic transmissions.

## Comparing many means with ANOVA

Undergraduate students taking an introductory statistics course at Boston University conducted a survey about GPA and major. We want to test if the mean GPA differs by major (4 groups).

```{r}
# loading the data from csv file
df <- read.csv("gpa_major.csv")
glimpse(df)

summary(df$gpa)
unique(df$major)


```

We assume that the data are independent within and between the groups and the data come from independent random samples.

\
We are going to get each group.

```{r}

Bio_df <- df %>% filter(major=="Biology")
Stat_df <- df %>% filter(major=="Statistics")
Eng_df <- df %>% filter(major=="Engineering")
Hist_df <- df %>% filter(major=="History")


summary(Bio_df)
summary(Stat_df)
summary(Eng_df)
summary(Hist_df)

```

We will make box plots and histograms of majors.

```{r}

ggplot(df, aes(x = major, y = gpa, fill = major)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "GPA Distribution by Major",
       x = "Major",
       y = "GPA") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

```{r}
ggplot(data=Bio_df, aes(x=gpa)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5)

ggplot(data=Stat_df, aes(x=gpa)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5)

ggplot(data=Eng_df, aes(x=gpa)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5)

ggplot(data=Hist_df, aes(x=gpa)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5)

```

Fit one-way ANOVA and show table up to the F statistic

```{r}
# H_0 : mu_bio = mu_stat = mu_eng = mu_hist
# H_a : At least one mean is different from the others


fit <- aov(gpa ~ major, data = df)
anova_tab <- anova(fit)
print(anova_tab)


### equivalently 
fit <- lm(gpa ~ major, data = df)
anova_tab2 <- anova(fit)
print(anova_tab2)
```

Based on the p-value of 0.01544, which is less than the 0.05 significance level, we reject the null hypothesis. This provides strong evidence that there is a significant difference in mean GPA among at least some of the four majors.
